title: Modulus graphs and transformations
what_it_asks: You are given a modulus function such as $y = a|x - b| + c$ or $y = |\mathrm{f}(x)|$, or a curve with labelled points. You are asked to sketch it, find the vertex or intercepts, solve a modulus equation or inequality, or say where points go under a transformation. The idea is that the modulus reflects any part of the graph below the $x$-axis, and that each transformation changes coordinates in a predictable way.
typical_structure: Usually two to four parts, and most questions come with a diagram. Early parts are short: state a point, sketch a curve or write down coordinates. Later parts are longer: solve an equation or inequality, or find a value of $k$ for intersections. Later parts often lean on your sketch or on points found earlier, so a wrong early sketch can cause trouble further on. Totals are usually around six to eight marks, though some questions run much longer.
mark_pattern: Most of the marks are independent marks. Sketch and transformation parts are typically B1 B1 or B1 B1 B1: one for the correct shape, then one each for the required coordinates or intercepts. Single-mark parts are often a lone B1 for a stated point or value. Algebraic parts follow M1 A1, sometimes M1 A1 A1, or M1 A1 M1 A1 when there are two stages. The first M1 is for removing the modulus by taking a branch or setting up the equation. The A1 is for the correct value. A later dM1 depends on that first method. A B1ft sometimes appears when you must use your own earlier points.

where_marks_leak.text: You give the final value to the wrong number of decimal places or significant figures. The final A1 is lost even though the method was right, so keep full accuracy and round only on the last line.
You confuse $y = |\mathrm{f}(x)|$ with $y = \mathrm{f}(|x|)$ and reflect the wrong part of the graph. The shape B1 is lost, and the B1 marks for the coordinates that follow from it often go too.
You leave out or misplace the intercepts or the vertex on the sketch. Each missing coordinate pair costs its own B1, because the marker needs to see the values on the axes.
You draw a rounded curve where the modulus gives a sharp corner, or the wrong end behaviour. The shape B1 is lost.
You solve both branches and keep a value that does not satisfy the original equation. The final A1 is lost, so substitute back or check against your sketch.

write_to_earn: Sketch first and label the vertex and every axis intercept with coordinates, since each is usually a separate B1.
Write each branch of the modulus as its own equation before solving, so the method mark is secure.
For a transformation, write the image of each given point in turn, not just the final curve.
Substitute each solution back into the original modulus equation and cross out any that fail.
Give exact values or the stated accuracy only on the final line, keeping full accuracy before then.
